definitions.explanation: To call someone to come; to summon a person.
To bring forth or evoke (feelings, memories, etc.).

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}に{職員室|しょくいんしつ}に{呼|よ}び{出|だ}された。
examples.english: I was summoned to the staff room by the teacher.

examples.japanese: タクシーを{呼|よ}び{出|だ}してください。
この{歌|うた}は{懐|なつ}かしい{思|おも}い{出|で}を{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す。

notes:
{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す is a compound godan verb from {呼|よ}ぶ (to call) + {出|だ}す (out).

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle: 〜を{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {先生|せんせい}に{呼|よ}び{出|だ}される: to be summoned by the teacher
- {上司|じょうし}に{呼|よ}び{出|だ}される: to be called in by one's boss
- タクシーを{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す: to call a taxi
- {思|おも}い{出|で}を{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す: to evoke memories

USAGE:
The passive form {呼|よ}び{出|だ}される is very common, especially in school/work contexts where being summoned often implies trouble.

COMPUTING:
{関数|かんすう}を{呼|よ}び{出|だ}す: to call a function
